lessons.briefing:
Hanging a door: plane to clearance (often about 2–3 mm as taught — follow the spec), mark hinge gains from the hanging stile, chop or router to the leaf thickness so the hinge sits flush. Screws in the frame must bite — pack or longer screws into studs if the lining is hollow.

Locks: mortise at the right height, keep aligned, and do not split the stile. Handle sets have a backset. Test the latch before you call it done.

Moisture movement: a door hung in the rains on wet timber binds at the head the next week. Ease the high spot after checking hinges have not sunk. Advise sealing all faces, including the bottom edge, or the job comes back.

Ironmongery on exterior work should be the specified corrosion resistance. Bright mild screws on a coastal door rust and seize.

lessons.briefing:
Circular saws, bandsaws, and thicknessers remove fingers faster than any other college machine. Guards on, riving knife on, push sticks for short pieces, and never stand in the kickback line. Unplug to change blades. Dust extraction is health, not comfort.

Joints: housing, mortise and tenon, haunch, dovetail as taught. Dry fit. Shoulders must seat. Glue is not gap-filler for a 4 mm error. Cramp with protection blocks; check square as you tighten — frames rack.

Mark waste with hatching. Cut on the waste side of the line. A tenon that is too tight will split the mortise; too loose will fail when the glue dries.

Stop the machine fully before you clear offcuts. That sentence is in every accident report.
lessons.briefingSw: Guards na push sticks. Usisimame kwenye mstari wa kickback. Dry fit viungo. Gundi si filler. Zima mashine kabisa kabla ya kuondoa offcuts.

lessons.briefing:
Joinery is accurate only if every cut is taken from known faces. Mark face side and face edge. Squares sit on those faces. A rod or cutting list beats measuring each piece from the last mistake.

Saws: a sharp saw is safer than a dull one. Support the waste so the last fibre does not splinter. Chisels: two hands, no body behind the point, knockers — not your palm on a stuck mortise in a hurry.

Moisture: wet timber moves after you hang a door. Store stickers, off the ground, as taught. Write the job size after checking the opening, not from the drawing alone if the site is out.

Assessors look at your marks. Faint, confused lines produce confused joints.
